rationale: Legitimate Q1 beat ($0.32 vs $0.18) and return to +3% organic growth from -13% prior quarter, strong China share gains (5 of last 6 quarters), operating margin +300bps to 7.3%. But management explicitly reaffirmed (not raised) full-year guidance despite the beat, flagging tougher H2 comps in China and Travel Retail, persistent Western Europe weakness, and $100M tariff headwind that hits P&L in Q2-Q4 (not Q1). Tax rate elevated at 40.5%. 7.3% operating margin still far below 'solid double digit' target. CEO tone hedged: 'lot of volatility,' 'extremely dynamic,' 'still very subdued.' Turnaround credible but back-half compression risk and subdued tone on reacceleration keep this balanced rather than conviction-continue.

Clean beat-and-raise: EPS $7.57 vs $6.97 expectations, bookings +12%, revenue +9%, EBITDA margin +2pts. Raised both Q4 and full-year guidance. Strongest US room night growth in 3+ years, B2B +26% (17th consecutive double-digit quarter), advertising +16%. CEO confirmed 'continued momentum in October' and longer booking windows / longer stays (stronger consumer signals). B2C margins hit 41% with direct sales & marketing actually down 4%. Direct confident Q&A, multiple legs of margin expansion identified for 2026. 22% share reduction over 3 years via buybacks amplifies EPS. All three brands (Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo) accelerating. Multiple reinforcing positives with no meaningful red flags.

EPS beat $0.54 vs $0.45, costs better than guided at $1.13/lb. Major structural tailwind: ~$1.25/lb US COMEX premium from 50% copper tariff implies ~$1.7B annual financial benefit on US sales. H2 copper sales +10% vs H1. Smelter started up a month ahead of schedule. Morenci leach field trial progressing. Copper thesis: governments focused on critical minerals, AI/electrification demand secular, exchange inventories globally low. Yellow flags: 15% reduction in 2025 gold production from Grasberg ore grade model recalibration (management frames as timing/flow, not reserve impairment, and long-range plans unchanged); full-year unit cost ticked up $0.05 to $1.55 due to lower gold volumes. Q&A answers direct and technical. Net: strong positive with structural tariff tailwind, offset only partially by gold timing issue.

Exceptional across every dimension. EPS $8.25 doubled YoY, 33% same-store revenue growth, EBITDA +74% to $414M (first-ever quarter over $400M). Backlog at record $9.4B (+65% YoY, +$1.3B sequential all same-store). Gross margin 24.8% vs 21.1% prior year, both segments expanded. Technology/data center now 42% of revenue (up from 32%). Dividend raised 20%. Two acquisitions closed Oct 1 adding $200M+ annual revenue. Free cash flow $519M in quarter. 2026 guidance: low-to-mid teens same-store revenue growth. Management: 'opportunities, pipeline is still robust... no let up at all.' Direct Q&A throughout. Clear beat-and-raise with massive secular tailwind (data center buildout) and 62% higher same-store backlog entering final quarter. Strong conviction momentum continues.

EPS $3.18 above high end of guidance. Reconciliation bill + FEOC provisions materially strengthen FSLR's competitive position vs Chinese/Southeast Asian crystalline silicon. July bookings surged 2.1 GW post-bill signing with pricing of $0.32-0.33/W (above backlog ASP of $0.299). Multiple forward catalysts: 232 polysilicon investigation, UFLPA enforcement, new AD/CVD petitions (Laos/Indonesia/India). Pipeline 83.3 GW with 20.1 GW mid-to-late stage. Louisiana facility commissioning, CuRe/perovskite progressing. Negatives are real but addressed: 1.1 GW terminations in Q2 (<2% of backlog), $394M overdue receivables, tariff headwinds of $150-200M combined on BOM + finished goods, international business dilutive without tariff recoveries, underutilization charges $95-180M, EPS midpoint unchanged (with $0.70 drag from 45X credit sale assumption). Management direct and confident on long-term setup; near-term noisy. Net positive given FSLR is the clearest US policy beneficiary with multiple catalysts stacking through 2H.
